6 simple tweaks I use to get two days of battery from my Galaxy Watch 9

Battery life continues to be a struggle for Galaxy Watch owners.

•

•

•

Rushil Agrawal / Android Authority

Preferred Source

Google Discover

When the Samsung Galaxy Watch 9 was first announced, one of the features that excited me most was the larger battery. I actually upgraded to a 44mm model, so I was expecting a significant improvement in battery life compared to my 40mm Watch 8. However, in practice, I found that it lasted roughly the same amount of time.

Even so, I don’t have to charge it daily, and that’s thanks to a handful of tweaks that get me two days instead. These tweaks balance usability with battery saving so that you don’t give up too many features in the quest to extend battery life.

Readers' poll

Do you think the Samsung Galaxy Watch 9 delivers enough battery life?

0 votes

Turn off the Always On Display

Megan Ellis / Android Authority

When you set up the Galaxy Watch 9, the Always On Display (AOD) is enabled by default. However, this is by far the most battery-hungry feature. When I have it enabled, my watch needs to be charged daily. So if you’re like me and prefer to keep charging limited, this is the first setting you should change.

The difference in your battery life is apparent. After enabling the Always On Display for less than 30 minutes, it had already consumed 0.9% of my battery. Meanwhile, Samsung Health, which had been running for nearly 22 hours since the last charge, had only used 4.3% of my battery.

Disabling the AOD makes the biggest difference to your battery life without sacrificing much.

To disable the feature using your watch, swipe down and tap the watch icon.

You can also disable it in your Galaxy Wearable app:

1. Tap the hamburger icon at the bottom right.

2. Select Display > Always On Display. Make sure the toggle is turned off.

There are other ways to improve the battery life on your watch, but just disabling this feature will give you the largest gains.

Keep notifications limited to essential apps

Megan Ellis / Android Authority

The display is the biggest drain on your Watch 9’s battery, but background activity adds up too. That’s why I limit which apps I receive notifications from on my watch — it prevents my screen from waking unnecessarily, my watch doesn’t have to trigger vibrations as much, and it means I have fewer apps syncing in the background. I also only show notifications when my phone is not in use.

I always make sure to only enable notifications from the apps that are most important to me to reduce battery drain.

The app notifications you want to enable will depend on which apps you prioritize the most. I only want to see notifications from Slack, WhatsApp, Samsung Health, Google Calendar, and Google Messages. I’ve disabled everything else. I also make sure to manage notifications within each app so that I only receive alerts from certain channels or people, rather than large groups.

To manage the notifications you receive on your Watch 9:

1. Open Galaxy Wearable and select the hamburger icon at the bottom right.

2. Select Notifications > App notifications.

3. Toggle the apps you want to allow or disallow.

Under the Notifications panel, you can also select Show phone notifications on watch > Show alerts when not in use to only receive notifications when you’re not using your phone.

Uninstall unused apps

Megan Ellis / Android Authority

Even if you’re not using an app, it might still contribute to battery drain on your watch. I noticed this with an app I used to download Galaxy Watch 9 faces, even though I didn’t have a face from the app currently installed.

This is where the Galaxy Wearable’s Battery menu comes in handy. It lets you check which apps have used up battery power since your last charge. I recommend checking this tab to see if you have any unused apps draining your battery in the background.

Get rid of apps you're no longer using so that they don't contribute to battery drain.

You can access this menu in Galaxy Wearable using the following steps:

1. Tap the hamburger icon at the bottom right.

2. Go to Battery and scroll down to Usage since last full charge.

Here you can check which apps are the biggest culprits when it comes to battery drain.

To uninstall an app:

1. Select the hamburger icon > Apps.

2. Choose the app you want to uninstall from the list.

3. Tap the Uninstall button.

Choose a watch face with static elements

Megan Ellis / Android Authority

While you may be tempted to load your watch face with as much data as possible, along with animated visuals, doing so can drain more battery power. In fact, if you’re downloading a third-party watch face from the Google Play Store, the storefront now flags watch face apps that drain battery.

On third-party watch face storefronts like Facer, you will also see the impact a specific face has on battery life. Faces that sync a significant amount of data or that include animated visuals are usually the ones that impact battery life the most. Meanwhile, simple watch faces with few complications impact battery life the least.

Switching to an interactive, animated, or data-heavy watch face can reduce battery life.

Unfortunately, native Galaxy Watch faces don’t show details of the battery consumption of a specific watch face. In my own experience, switching from a Photos watch face to one that features Live wallpapers consumed more battery life. My Photos wallpaper consumed 0.6% of my watch’s battery life over 41 hours. The live wallpapers watch face consumed the same amount in 10 minutes after switching through five wallpapers.

Use a darker background

Megan Ellis / Android Authority

Even if you use a relatively static watch face, using a darker background also improves battery life. I tested this with my Photos watch face, switching from a light photo of my cats to a darker one featuring my black cat. I made the change after seeing the suggestion in the Galaxy Wearable app when choosing a watch face.

After switching to the darker background, I noticed that this added around four to five hours extra to my watch’s battery life. I also have Adaptive Brightness turned on so that my watch adjusts to the environment. While Adaptive Brightness didn’t make a massive difference on its own, it’s the type of tweak that you implement with other changes. These changes then add up and can add a considerable amount to your watch’s battery life.

Switch off Raise wrist to wake

Megan Ellis / Android Authority

Raise wrist to wake is another feature that drains battery life, but its effect will depend on how much you use the feature. When I disabled it, I got around another three hours of battery life. However, it was also an annoying change to make because it was so different from how I was used to using my watch.

I would recommend this change for people who don’t mind tapping their smartwatch to see notifications, or people who find that they accidentally trigger the feature fairly often. When I made all of these tweaks to my Galaxy Watch, I added an extra day to its battery life without sacrificing the health features that are important to me.

The changes you make will depend on the features that are most important to you.

A few other tricks that improve battery life include:

• Measuring heart rate every 10 minutes while still, rather than continuously.

• Switching to manual stress measurements.

• Turning off blood oxygen and skin temperature detection while sleeping.

• Turning off Auto detect workouts.

However, you’ll need to decide which features you’re willing to part with. I currently use heart rate monitoring every 10 minutes over continuous monitoring, but I keep blood oxygen and skin temperature detection enabled because I need them for the Vitals feature. Without the auto detection of workouts, I’d also forget to track my exercise completely. The best battery-saving tweaks for you will depend on what you use your watch for.

items.summary: How does a 92% discount on a Galaxy S26 Ultra sound?
items.body:

Mobile

Samsung (accidentally) sold the Galaxy S26 Ultra for just $125 in Japan

How does a 92% discount on a Galaxy S26 Ultra sound?

•

Nov 27, 2026 — 4:52 AM ET

•

•

Shimul Sood / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Amazon Japan briefly listed the 256GB Galaxy S26 Ultra for ~$125, down from its regular price of $1,504.

• Several buyers have confirmed that they received their orders, suggesting that Amazon honored the deal.

There’s no shortage of great Black Friday deals today, with the Pixel 11 series, Nothing Phone 3, and Galaxy Z8 foldables all receiving price cuts today. However, it looks like some lucky customers in Japan got the best deal of them all.

Amazon Japan briefly offered the 256GB Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra at a 92% discount (h/t: tokka_news_2026 and yeux1122). This discount took the phone from 239,800 yen (~$1,504) to just 20,185 yen (~$125). The promotion, which applied to the Sky Blue model, is no longer available, suggesting that this may have been an accident.

Naver blogger Yeux1122

Nevertheless, several users chimed in on X to confirm that they received their order. So it looks like Amazon Japan indeed honored the discounted price.

This was clearly the best Black Friday deal, even if it was an apparent accident. For everyone else, the phone is still available on Amazon US for $1,049.99, which is $350 off the recommended price.

Expect a Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy chipset, a 5,000mAh battery, 60W wired charging, and an S Pen with an integrated slot. Other notable features include a 200MP main camera, a 50MP 5x camera, an IP68 rating, wireless charging, and seven years of major OS updates.

items.title: We tested Samsung’s private Galaxy AI cloud on One UI 9.5 beta, and it made AI select smarter
items.summary: Running AI select through Samsung SPAC on a Galaxy S26 Ultra produced an accurate calendar entry that didn't need edits.

Mobile

We tested Samsung’s private Galaxy AI cloud on One UI 9.5 beta, and it made AI select smarter

Running AI select through Samsung SPAC on a Galaxy S26 Ultra produced an accurate calendar entry that didn't need edits.

•

Nov 27, 2026 — 4:02 AM ET

•

•

Stephen Radochia / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• We got Samsung’s private AI cloud, referred to as “SPAC” in the code, working with AI select on a Galaxy S26 Ultra running One UI 9.5 Beta 1, producing more accurate calendar event extraction than its standard processing.

• Code references show SPAC supports Google’s Gemma 4 and Alibaba’s Qwen 3.6 (used in our test) and appears to route encrypted requests through a third-party relay to hide user identity.

• In our test, SPAC only pulled one event out of the five listed, but Samsung’s code indicates multi-event support. It also suggests photo editing, live translation, and writing tools could adopt SPAC next.

Yesterday, we reported that Samsung is building a private cloud for Galaxy AI. The system, called “SPAC” in Samsung’s code, appears to closely follow Apple’s Private Cloud Compute. At the time, SPAC wasn’t switched on for our Galaxy S26 Ultra. Now we’ve managed to get it running, and the result is better than what Galaxy AI does today.

APK teardown

This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

You're reading an Android Authority exclusive story you won’t find anywhere else. An APK teardown helps predict features that may arrive on a service in the future based on work-in-progress code. However, it is possible that such predicted features may not make it to a public release. More Authority Insights →

AI select used SPAC to add an event to our calendar

AI select, part of the Samsung Capture app, can pull details from your screen and suggest actions, like adding an event to your calendar. We pointed it at a Google search result listing upcoming Lollapalooza dates and tapped “Add event.”

On One UI 9.5 Beta 1 on the Galaxy S26 Ultra, this normally opens Samsung Calendar with fields filled in from the selected text.

The result was a bit of a mess: the event was titled “Course Reservation” for some reason. It selected the Mumbai entry for the dates but added multiple locations to the location field. Clearly, the “Lollapalooza India” context was lost.

Once we managed to turn on SPAC for AI select, the same selection and tap took a different route.

AI select sent the selection to Samsung’s SPAC servers, and after a few noticeable seconds of processing (which were missing before), Samsung Capture showed its own “Add event” sheet with a cleaner entry: “Lollapalooza India,” January 23, 2027, at Mahalaxmi Race Course, Mumbai. AI select managed to get the correct title, date, and venue for the calendar entry, without any edits from our end.

Admittedly, the result wasn’t perfect. The page listed five Lollapalooza editions, and SPAC returned only the first, possibly either because of our device location (Mumbai) or simply because it was the first entry in the list. Samsung’s code supports adding several events at once, so this could change by the time the feature goes live for users.

SPAC’s privacy design appears to be in place

SPAC’s code describes several privacy layers, including a third-party relay that hides where a request comes from and a public-style record of Samsung’s server software. When AI select used SPAC, our phone did not look up Samsung’s AI server directly. That’s pretty much how this design is supposed to work: the phone sends the request to a relay, and the relay forwards the encrypted request to SPAC, so the AI server only sees the request, not who sent it.

The code lists Google’s Gemma 4 and Alibaba’s Qwen 3.6 as AI select’s two SPAC options, and our test used Qwen 3.6. Your phone will only send the model’s name with the request, so we can’t confirm which model actually answered.

What this means for Galaxy AI

Stephen Radochia / Android Authority

The demo is small, but it’s the first sign that Samsung’s private AI cloud is real and not just code in the platform. A Galaxy phone can already send it a request and get a useful answer, although all of this is still very much a beta.

If Samsung goes ahead, AI select could be one of the first Galaxy AI features to run on SPAC, with photo editing, live translation, and writing tools possibly following. It’s also not clear yet whether SPAC-powered features would be free or paid as part of Galaxy AI Premium.

We’ve reached out to Samsung for comment on SPAC and will update this article if we hear back.

items.summary: From specific settings to alternative emulators, here's what you can try on your non-Snapdragon device.

Gaming

Got a MediaTek, Exynos, or Pixel device? Here are 11 tips for emulation

From specific settings to alternative emulators, here's what you can try on your non-Snapdragon device.

•

Nov 27, 2026 — 4:00 AM ET

•

•

Nick Fernandez / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

There’s no shortage of emulators on Android, letting you play everything from Atari 2600 and NES games to PC and Nintendo Switch titles. We’ve even seen Xbox 360, PlayStation 3, and Switch 2 emulators in recent times.

It’s fair to say, though, that devices with Qualcomm Snapdragon chips are generally the best for emulation. Phones and handhelds with MediaTek, Google Tensor, or Samsung Exynos silicon often suffer from worse performance and compatibility with new emulators as a result. Thankfully, there are plenty of tips you can try if you’re struggling with emulation on your MediaTek-powered device, Exynos-toting Galaxy phone, or Google Pixel.

Readers' poll

What's the best tip for emulation on Android?

0 votes

1. Use Vulkan rather than OpenGL (or ANGLE)

Hadlee Simons / Android Authority

One of the most enduring tips for running emulators on non-Snapdragon devices is to switch the graphics renderer from OpenGL to Vulkan. Vulkan generally performs better than OpenGL, so you should get a speed boost by making the switch. This isn’t always the case, but it’s still one of the first things you should try if you’re having performance problems in an emulator.

It’s also worth noting that Samsung’s and Google’s chips don’t have great OpenGL support in the first place. Instead, they use a “wrapper” called ANGLE to translate OpenGL calls to Vulkan. Some emulators offer ANGLE as an option in their settings. If an emulator doesn’t, you can enable ANGLE via developer options and leave the emulator on the OpenGL renderer. Morphe v2.4.0 beats Google to bringing YouTube videos to your Android Auto screen

It only shows up when your vehicle is parked.

•

•

Hadlee Simons / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

TL;DR

• Morphe v2.4.0 is out, and it adds support for playing YouTube videos on Android Auto and other in-car entertainment platforms.

• YouTube shows up in the Android Auto launcher when the car is parked.

• Along with this, Morphe’s version of YouTube and YouTube Music also get a host of playability improvements.

Morphe is a popular open-source tool for modding popular Android apps to add features and remove ads from YouTube, YouTube Music, and other media streaming apps. In the last major update, it added 4K video downloads, surpassing download-quality limits even on the official YouTube app. Now, it’s out with another update that brings a host of changes to patched versions of Reddit, YouTube, and YouTube Music. One that truly stands out — and we hope isn’t blocked by Google — is the ability to play YouTube videos on Android Auto.

Release notes for version 2.40 of the Morphe app say a new patch now lets Morphe YouTube be seen as a “parked video app.” As a result, the app shows up in Android Auto’s app drawer, and you can watch videos directly while your vehicle isn’t moving. This is currently only available as an early access feature and also works with DriveDeck. Google itself has been working to bring a similar functionality to phones running Android 17 or newer by the end of the year. Currently, users can only listen to audio from YouTube videos on Android Auto, but the app must be controlled from the phone.

Meanwhile, another patch detects when the YouTube app is projected onto the car’s display and adjusts its layout for horizontal screens, while another one hides the navigation bar to utilize the space better. It also enables Android Auto alternatives such as DriveDeck, Gearslip, AARE, and Flywheel to browse YouTube Music’s library.

Along with this, the latest Morphe update brings several minor upgrades to both YouTube and YouTube Music that aren’t specific to Android Auto. These improvements include a new Ghost mode, similar to Incognito, where watched videos don’t show in your watch history or impact your recommendations. You can browse using Ghost mode for an entire session or launch just one video using the three-dot button — all this without having to sign out of your account.

Lyrics in YouTube Music now support a full-screen mode, along with support for custom fonts. You also get the option to disable gestures for changing tracks by swiping over the album art. Besides this, YouTube Music also gains a direct Sonos casting button that lets you stream audio directly to UPnP speakers from Sonos and other brands, so long as they’re on the same Wi-Fi.

Here's how much OnePlus could charge you for using ColorOS 17's AI features

Would you be willing to pay to use AI features built into your phone?

•

•

•

Dhruv Bhutani / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• OPPO has introduced three monthly AI subscription tiers for ColorOS 17 in India.

• The plans range from around $3 to $10 and will offer up to 100,000 credits per month.

• Only Live Translation, AI Photo Agent, and Transcription features will use credits, while other AI features remain free.

OnePlus recently confirmed that it will start imposing usage limits on some AI features in ColorOS 17. Users will have a free usage allowance, after which they can either pay for more usage or wait for their allowance to reset. However, the company hadn’t confirmed price details just yet. Well, we’re getting a clearer idea of its plans now.

According to a post on X by user Ashok Mor, OPPO has started offering subscription-based AI plans for ColorOS 17. There are three subscription tiers, per their post:

• Basic: Rs. 289/month (~$3/month) for 20,000 credits

• Pro: Rs. 579/month (~$6/month) for 50,000 credits

• Ultra: Rs. 959/month (~$10/month) for 100,000 credits

These credits are reportedly shared across three AI features: Live Translation, AI Photo Agent, and Transcription. Based on the post, the Basic plan will get you roughly 50 Photo Agent uses or 100 minutes of translation. The Pro plan bumps that up to 125 uses or 250 minutes, while the Ultra plan offers around 250 uses or 500 minutes.

@_techibee / X

You can also buy top-up credits if you run out of your monthly quota, with credit packs starting at Rs. 189 (~$2) for 10,000 credits. These credits are valid for one year. OPPO also seems to be running a limited-time offer that gives users 10,000 free credits per month for one year, so users can experiment with the AI features before deciding whether to subscribe.

Based on the screenshots in the post, it seems only the three AI features listed above will use AI credits. Other AI features in ColorOS 17 could remain available for free, at least for now. Neither OnePlus nor OPPO has officially announced a rollout or confirmed pricing for other regions. We have reached out to both companies for a statement and will update this post when we hear back.

items.summary: This charging reminder feature could even refer to your calendar entries for more personalized alerts.

Samsung phones can soon nudge you when you miss your usual charging window

This charging reminder feature could even refer to your calendar entries for more personalized alerts.

•

Nov 27, 2026 — 3:11 AM ET

•

•

Ryan Haines / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Samsung’s One UI 9.5 beta can apparently tell you when you’ve missed your usual charging time.

• This alert will show up in the Settings menu and will also show how many hours of battery life you have left.

• This feature could be very useful if you’re forgetful or busy.

Samsung recently launched the One UI 9.5 beta program, allowing Galaxy S26 owners to get their hands on the latest software before the stable release. We’ve already uncovered plenty of features, but it looks like the company has a convenient charging-related feature up its sleeve.

APK teardown

This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

You're reading an Android Authority exclusive story you won’t find anywhere else. An APK teardown helps predict features that may arrive on a service in the future based on work-in-progress code. However, it is possible that such predicted features may not make it to a public release. More Authority Insights →

We’ve dug into the Device Care app (v13.9.00.12) in One UI 9.5 and discovered that Samsung phones could soon issue an alert when you’ve missed your usual charging time. We can confirm that this alert will appear when the battery is at 20-30% capacity, your phone isn’t charging, and power-saving modes are disabled. Check out the string below.

Code

<string name="suggest_appbar_charging_description">You missed your usual charging time.</string>

We’ve also uncovered strings (seen below) which show that the alert could use events in your default calendar for context. More specifically, the alert could mention that your battery might be low for a workout, movie, meeting, or show/concert at a given time. If you don’t have a matching calendar event, then the feature will fall back to the alert message seen in the string above.

Code

<string name="suggest_appbar_exercise_description">Battery may be low for your workout at %s.</string> 
<string name="suggest_appbar_meeting_description">Battery may be low for your meeting at %s.</string> 
<string name="suggest_appbar_movie_description">Battery may be low for your movie at %s.</string> 
<string name="suggest_appbar_performance_description">Battery may be low for your %1$s at %2$s.</string>

So how does this actually work? Well, you’ll first need to enable Samsung’s personalized suggestions option and have a device with One UI 9.5. The phone will then identify your preferred charging window by learning from four weeks of charging history, as retained by the Smart suggestions app. The device will then check if the current hour falls within this preferred charging window, and display the alert if this is the case. The code suggests that if you dismiss the alert, it won’t come back again for 24 hours, even if all other conditions are met. Oddly enough, we also found evidence that Samsung can remotely turn off this card.

There’s no country check, while the evidence we’ve uncovered also suggests that it won’t be exclusive to the Galaxy S27 series. So this charging alert could potentially come to older Galaxy phones in many markets.

What could these charging alerts look like?

SamMobile also posted a screenshot showing off this alert. It’s unclear whether this feature is available in some capacity or if the outlet manually enabled it by tinkering with the software. Check out the image below.

SamMobile

This notification apparently pops up at the top of the Settings menu. It also includes a graphic showing how many hours of battery life you have left and how much usage time you’ll gain if you enable battery-saving mode.

I can see this proactive alert being very useful for people who either forget to charge their phones or those who are very busy. That battery life graphic should also help you make up your mind about whether you need to charge your device straight away.

Either way, this charging alert seems like a very sensible addition to One UI 9.5. We hope other Android OEMs copy Samsung and implement this in their own software skins.

items.summary: TCL CSOT showed off the future of display tech at DTC 2026.
items.body:

General technology

TCL CSOT unveils APEX and IJP OLED breakthroughs for the AI era at DTC 2026

TCL CSOT showed off the future of display tech at DTC 2026.

Brought to you by TCL CSOT

•

Nov 27, 2026 — 2:56 AM ET

•

TCL CSOT

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

A screen has a big impact on how a device feels to use. It determines how crisp text looks on your laptop, how smoothly fast-moving games appear on your monitor, how long your phone lasts on a charge, and whether the person next to you on the train can read your screen. OLED screens, in particular, need a lot of precision to manufacture, which is why they’re most often found only in higher-end phones, laptops, monitors, and tablets.

TCL CSOT, which makes and develops displays for many device manufacturers, is working on a method to build OLED panels by printing the materials onto them, which could help OLED get into more products.

At DTC 2026, its annual Global Display Tech-Ecosystem Conference in Wuhan, China, on November 13, TCL CSOT showcased its latest display tech: inkjet-printed OLED, a 500Hz gaming monitor, a 115-inch 16K screen that shows 3D without glasses, and more. They also took Android Authority on a tour of the Wuhan factory and the t12 production line, where they’re working on the IJP OLED. Here’s what you need to know.

How inkjet-printed OLED works

TCL CSOT

IJP OLED stands for inkjet-printed OLED. While traditional OLED manufacturing uses processes to deposit organic materials onto the display, IJP OLED uses specialized printers to place those materials precisely where they’re needed. The idea is similar to using a home inkjet printer, but the “ink” is made of organic materials that form a working OLED panel.

Printing the materials this way helps reduce waste and potentially lower manufacturing costs, which is a significant advantage for bringing OLED to a wider range of products in the future.

It also offers a picture-quality benefit. IJP OLED uses TCL CSOT’s Real Stripe RGB pixel arrangement, with separate red, green, and blue subpixels arranged in stripes. This design delivers sharper text and noticeably reduces color fringing around the edges of text and graphics compared with a conventional OLED panel.

TCL CSOT

Interview with Weiran Cao, Ph.D, at DTC 2026

With IJP OLED, we can reach 163 PPI on a 27-inch 4K display. For gaming displays, it can reach 218 PPI, with a 0.03 millisecond response time. People read a lot of text on monitors and laptops, so this is a benefit users can see every day.Weiran Cao, Ph.D, General Manager of IJP-OLED Middle Platform of TCL CSOT

TCL CSOT has already begun mass-producing IJP OLED panels, and several partner devices using this tech were featured at DTC 2026. The Lenovo Legion R9000P has a 16-inch IJP OLED panel with a 2,560×1,600 resolution, a 240Hz refresh rate, and 100% DCI-P3 coverage. Meanwhile, Lenovo’s ThinkVision P27UL-40 is the company’s first IJP OLED monitor for commercial use, with a 27-inch 4K display and 99% DCI-P3 coverage. The MSI Prestige 14 AI+ and MSI PRO MAX OLED 271UPJW12 also use TCL CSOT’s printed panels.

TCL CSOT has also introduced two new 14-inch IJP OLED notebook panels. One is less than 0.66mm thick, weighs under 66g, and has a reflectance of less than 1%. The other eliminates the cover glass, using a hardened polarizer with an 8H rating instead, but it still feels like glass to the touch, whether you use a finger or a stylus.

A 500Hz gaming monitor and a 115-inch 3D TV display

TCL CSOT

TCL CSOT showed off a 27-inch QHD gaming monitor featuring an IJP OLED panel with an oxide backplane, and supporting refresh rates of up to 500Hz. TCL CSOT says it’s the first display to use in-panel compensation for high refresh rates. It helps maintain picture quality and runs in real time in the background, so there’s no need for the periodic power-off cycles used by conventional methods.

Real Stripe RGB keeps edges sharp, with a response time under 1ms. The 500Hz refresh rate is designed for competitive gaming, keeping moving targets in fast-paced shooters crisp and easy to track.

TCL CSOT

The 115-inch display has a native 16K resolution of 15,360×7,680, and TCL CSOT says it is the world’s highest image quality 16K 2D/3D-compatible light-field TV display. Its light-field optical architecture addresses the viewing-angle limitations of conventional glasses-free 3D, offering a 90-degree viewing angle or more, extended depth of field, and support for multiple viewers, so you don’t have to sit in one specific spot. The 3D light-field resolution reaches up to 8K, and the screen can switch between 2D and 3D, with TCL CSOT claiming there’s no loss in 2D picture quality.

The recommended viewing distance is 2–4m (6.5–13ft), making it well suited for private theatres, digital museums, interactive gaming, and premium showrooms. It’s an impressive display, though it’s unlikely to find its way into living rooms anytime soon.

More efficient and more private mobile displays

TCL CSOT

The 6.36-inch blue phosphorescent OLED may have been one of the most practical displays at DTC 2026. TCL CSOT says it’s the first smartphone OLED display to use a blue phosphorescent material system, which they say delivers roughly 40% higher luminous efficiency and around 20% lower electroluminescent power consumption at the same brightness.

The display is a major power draw, so the battery-life improvements are definitely exciting. Paired with the larger batteries introduced in newer handsets, more efficient screens could significantly increase the time you can use your device between charges. TCL CSOT is also working to refine materials and manufacturing processes to extend device lifetimes and bring blue phosphorescent displays to more devices.

TCL CSOT

The World’s First Full-Angle Lossless Privacy OLED Tablet Display(10.95″) helps keep your screen private from people nearby. Its dual-pixel architecture and pixel-level light-path control provide 360-degree active privacy while keeping the view clear from the front.

APEX and AI for Real

TCL CSOT

All of these technologies are part of APEX, TCL CSOT’s advanced display technology brand, created with picture quality, eye comfort, and sustainability in mind. APEX is built on four pillars: Amazing Display Experience, Protective of Eye Health, Eco-friendly to Build and Use, and Unlimited Imaginative Potential.

AI for Real was another major focus at DTC 2026. TCL’s strategy is to bring AI out of the lab and into everyday life. For TCL CSOT, a key part of that vision is Display for AI — advancing display technology so AI-powered devices can deliver a better experience. Whatever an AI assistant does on your phone or laptop, the screen is where you see the results and respond. That means better displays can make AI features feel more useful in your day-to-day life.

Know more about TCL CSOT at DTC 2026

TCL CSOT

At DTC 2026, TCL CSOT showed off its progress on several fronts. IJP OLED is moving beyond the demo stage and toward mass production, while gaming panels are advancing toward 500Hz. The company also showcased a 115-inch glasses-free 3D screen, along with new mobile panels that use less power and help keep your screen private. Bringing these efforts together is AI, which is helping TCL CSOT design displays much faster. And the great news is that many of these features are already in everyday use.

TCL CSOT makes panels for other device makers, so you can find its technology in products from a range of brands. IJP OLED is already featured in Lenovo and MSI laptops and monitors showcased at DTC 2026. The other displays are currently technology demonstrations, with no retail timelines announced yet. You can find more information about TCL CSOT’s display technology on its website.

Mobile

OnePlus 15 and 15R ColorOS 17 update adds auto PC unlocking, smarter photo storage, and more

ColorOS users are catching up with their OxygenOS counterparts.

•

Nov 27, 2026 — 2:06 AM ET

•

•

Tushar Mehta / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• OnePlus is rolling out a ColorOS 17 update to the OnePlus 15 and 15R that adds automatic PC unlocking through the O Plus Connect app.

• The update also lets users free up storage by removing backed-up photos, customize image quality and resolution, and connect their phone and tablet to the same PC at the same time.

• Both phones get Calculator, Translate, and privacy improvements, alongside the November 2026 security patch.

Earlier this month, OnePlus rolled out an OxygenOS 16 update that lets your phone automatically unlock your PC when connecting remotely. ColorOS users missed out on this feature at the time, receiving translation improvements instead. That’s changing with the latest ColorOS 17 update for the OnePlus 15 and 15R, which brings automatic PC unlocking, November 2026 security patches, and several other useful additions.

With the update, O Plus Connect can use a saved password to automatically unlock your computer during a remote connection, saving you the trouble of entering it manually. To set this up, tap the More icon on the floating ball during a remote connection, select Unlock PC, and enable “Automatically unlock when connected.” The update also lets you connect your phone and tablet to the same PC at the same time.

OnePlus is also making it easier to manage photo storage. While the company integrated Google Photos support into its native gallery app back in 2024, the latest update adds a handy storage management tool. Once your photos are backed up to the cloud, you can remove the local copies to free up space without losing the backups. You can also choose the resolution and image quality when saving edited photos, letting you create smaller files for sharing.

Shimul Sood / Android Authority

The Calculator app now displays previous calculations on its main screen, allowing you to easily resume them. It also has a revised button layout and better-organized unit conversion tools. The Translate app also picks up some new superpowers: it now provides more detailed word lookups, including pronunciation, grammar, and usage examples, and adapts sentence translations to the appropriate writing style.

Samsung Messages could soon find, send, and forward texts for you

The app's development is far from over.

TL;DR

• Samsung Messages version 16.3.27.7 is rolling out in South Korea with groundwork for hands-free message management.

• The update also hints at smarter message searches and the ability to check how received photos were created or edited.

• Similar capabilities were spotted in China in September, but global versions of Samsung Messages still lack these additions.

Samsung may have shut down its Messages app in the US in July, but that hasn’t stopped the company from developing new features for users elsewhere. The latest update rolling out in South Korea suggests Samsung is preparing its texting app for a future where AI assistants can do much more than help you write messages.

As Sam Updater spotted, Samsung Messages version 16.3.27.7 introduces support for 10 functions that AI assistants such as Gemini could use to interact directly with the app. These include drafting, sending, replying to, forwarding, searching for, and deleting messages, as well as looking up contacts.

Rather than opening Samsung Messages and scrolling through conversations to find a discount code a retailer sent you last week, for example, you could simply ask your AI assistant to find it. Similarly, you could ask it to find a particular message and forward it to someone without navigating the app yourself.

The additions are particularly interesting given our recent discovery of Samsung Galaxy Claw, an upcoming AI experience that could perform tasks on your behalf across several apps, including Messages.

The update also lays the groundwork for smarter message searches that understand the meaning of your queries rather than relying solely on matching keywords. Additionally, there’s evidence of support for Content Credentials, a feature that Google Messages already offers to help users determine how received media was created or edited, including whether AI was involved.

Joe Maring / Android Authority

However, downloading the latest Samsung Messages update doesn’t necessarily mean you can start using all these features today. The findings come from an analysis of the app’s code, and the features haven’t been demonstrated in action.

There’s also the question of availability. The update is reportedly being offered to select Galaxy phones running One UI 9.0 in South Korea, including Ultra models dating back to the Galaxy S23. China received similar groundwork in September, but even users running the newer One UI 9.5 beta in Europe and India are still on an older version of the app without these additions.

While there’s no indication that Samsung plans to reverse its decision to discontinue Messages in the US, it’s clear that the app’s development is far from over in markets where it remains available.

• It will also feature a 4.7-inch 4:3 display with a 120Hz refresh rate.

ANBERNIC already has several Android handhelds in its portfolio, and the company isn’t shying away from adding more. After announcing the yet-to-be-released RG DDS, ANBERNIC has now started teasing a new vertical handheld: the RG 47G1.

In a new YouTube video, ANBERNIC teased the upcoming RG 47G1 and shared a few key details about what we’ll find under the hood. For starters, the RG 47G1 will feature a 4.7-inch display with a 1,280 x 960 pixel resolution and a 120Hz refresh rate. It will also pack in the Snapdragon G1 Gen 2 chipset, which we’ve seen on the ANBERNIC RG 55G1, and a 5,500mAh battery with an active cooling system. The teaser also showcases the handheld in three colors: Pika Yellow, Retro Purple, and Black.

ANBERNIC hasn’t said anything about when the RG 47G1 could be released or how much it could cost. However, based on the specs we’ve seen so far, it seems like the RG 47G1 will be an RG 477V with a Snapdragon chipset replacing the Dimensity 8300. We’ve already seen the Snapdragon G1 Gen 2’s performance on the RG 55G1 and the Retroid Pocket Classic, and it’s an entry-level chip that performs quite well in emulation, so we’re expecting performance in line with those devices, and hopefully a similar price.

That said, it’s worth noting that rising memory prices could play a role in the RG 47G1’s pricing when it is released. Hopefully, it won’t go so high that it approaches the RG 477V’s price, which would put it in dangerous territory.

• Pantone’s 2027 Color of the Year, Aqua Splash (PANTONE 14-4812), has leaked ahead of its official announcement.

• Well-known leaker Evan Blass spotted the shade listed on Pantone’s own website, potentially giving us a clue about Motorola’s next special-edition phone.

• Motorola has launched smartphones in Pantone’s annual Color of the Year every year since 2022.

Motorola could have another colourful smartphone launch lined up for 2027. Pantone’s upcoming Color of the Year 2027, Aqua Splash (PANTONE 14-4812), has leaked ahead of its official announcement and Motorola might already be preparing a phone in the new shade.

Evan Blass spotted Aqua Splash listed on Pantone’s website, specifically its online shop page. The listing appears to have revealed the colour ahead of Pantone’s official announcement, giving us an early clue about what Motorola could be planning for its next Color of the Year smartphone.

Aqua Splash is a refreshing blue-green shade with an aquatic feel. While Pantone hasn’t officially confirmed the selection yet, its 2027 Color of the Year announcement is scheduled for December 3.

Motorola has made Pantone’s Color of the Year a smartphone tradition

C. Scott Brown / Android Authority

If you’ve followed Motorola’s smartphone launches over the past few years, you’ll know that the company has maintained a multi-year partnership with Pantone, using its colours across its smartphone portfolio and regularly bringing the annual Color of the Year to its devices.

The tradition started in 2022 with the Motorola Edge 30 Neo, which arrived in Very Peri, Pantone’s Color of the Year for that year. Motorola followed it up with the Edge 30 Fusion in Viva Magenta in 2023.

In 2024, the company brought Peach Fuzz to devices including the Razr 40 Ultra and Edge 40 Neo. Its 2025 lineup continued the trend with Mocha Mousse editions of the Razr 50 Ultra and Edge 50 Neo.

More recently, Motorola introduced the Edge 70 in Cloud Dancer, Pantone’s 2026 Color of the Year. The special edition even featured Swarovski crystals, showing that Motorola is increasingly treating these launches as design and lifestyle collaborations rather than straightforward colour refreshes.

For now, we don’t know which Motorola smartphone that could arrive in Aqua Splash. It could be a new Razr or Edge series device, or another model altogether. Motorola also hasn’t officially announced any plans for an Aqua Splash smartphone.

We’ll have to wait for Pantone’s official announcement and Motorola’s subsequent plans to find out is a device will actually adorn this color, and if this is indeed Pantone’s Color of the Year for next year.

items.body:

Mobile

Android just had one of its worst quarters, and Apple is benefiting

Android just recorded its lowest-ever share for a third quarter, with Apple's iOS bucking the trend.

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 10:41 PM ET

•

•

Stephen Radochia / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Android accounted for 74% of global smartphone sales in Q3 2026, down five points from a year ago and its lowest-ever share for a third quarter, per Counterpoint Research.

• iOS climbed to a record Q3 share of 21% as iPhone sales grew year-on-year, even as the overall market shrank 16%.

• HarmonyOS held at 5% globally and took 22% of China’s market, with HUAWEI growing 12% while China’s market shrank 10%.

The memory shortage has been dragging down phone sales all year, and new data shows it may be hurting Android more than its rivals.

According to Counterpoint Research, global smartphone sales fell 16% year-on-year in Q3 2026, a sharper drop than the 11% decline seen in Q2. Android’s share of those sales slipped to 74%, down from 79% in Q3 2025. That’s the lowest share Android has ever posted in a third quarter, though it’s still a touch above the 72% it hit in Q4 2025, when new iPhones typically give Apple a seasonal bump.

Counterpoint blames the RAM supply crisis, which has hit entry-level phones the hardest and pushed up prices in higher tiers. Because Android phones span every price segment, including the budget end where the squeeze has been worst, the platform has been more exposed to the slowdown than iOS. The firm says flagship launches from OPPO, vivo, and Xiaomi, along with Samsung’s latest foldables, helped soften the blow.

iPhones are bucking the trend

Shimul Sood / Android Authority

Apple, meanwhile, is having a good year in a bad market. iOS reached 21% of global sales in Q3 2026, its highest-ever share for a third quarter. iPhone sales actually grew 2% year-on-year while the overall market shrank 16%. Counterpoint credits the iPhone 18 Pro series, which it says outperformed the iPhone 17 Pro series, and notes that demand held up despite price increases across the iPhone lineup.

Meanwhile, HUAWEI’s HarmonyOS held steady at 5% of global sales. In China, it captured 22% of the market as the company’s sales grew 12% year-on-year, even as China’s overall market shrank 10%. The Enjoy 90 Pro Max, Nova 16, and Mate 80 series led the way, though Counterpoint warns that HUAWEI’s September price hikes could slow that momentum next quarter. HarmonyOS’s China share is down slightly from the record 24% it hit in Q2.

How Android fared in the US and other major markets

Here’s how the three markets Counterpoint tracks broke down in Q3 2026:

In the US, iOS pulled back ahead with 54% of sales, up from a near-even 51% in Q2, though Android’s 46% is still a point better than its 45% in Q3 2025. In China, Android recovered slightly to 60% from 58% in Q2, as HarmonyOS dipped. India remains firmly Android territory at 92%, unchanged from a year ago.

The bigger picture isn’t great for Android makers. Most major brands have reportedly cut their 2027 shipment targets, with vivo and Xiaomi trimming theirs by roughly a quarter, while Apple’s reported cut is far smaller. With memory prices not expected to ease until late 2027 at the earliest, budget Android phones, the segment that has historically powered Android’s dominance, look set to stay under pressure for a while yet.

In a recent AMA on the OnePlus Community forum, OnePlus revealed that it’s exploring plans to bring its native dialer to more markets. Many OnePlus phones ship with Google Phone, while users in markets like India have access to the company’s own calling app, complete with features such as call recording without an audible announcement, AI-powered call summaries, and real-time translations. More users could eventually ditch Google’s dialer, although availability, including call recording support, will depend on the device and region.

While some features will remain free, others will have free usage limits. Once you exhaust your allowance, you’ll have two options: pay for additional usage or wait for your allowance to reset. The company hasn’t specified how much additional usage will cost or how frequently these allowances will reset.

The feature lets you edit photos using natural language commands, much like Google Photos’ Help Me Edit. Meanwhile, AI Mind Pilot availability will vary by device, software version, and region. The company is also evaluating whether it can bring 3D and AI Motion Wallpapers to more phones.

OPPO

Music lovers wondering why lyrics aren’t showing up on their lock screens may have their streaming apps to blame. ColorOS 17 already supports the functionality, but music apps need to share lyrics with the system. OnePlus is working with app developers to expand compatibility.

Meanwhile, those experiencing increased battery drain or overheating after updating are advised to give their phones time to complete background optimizations. OnePlus hasn’t promised better battery life across all devices, but it says ColorOS 17 includes improvements to reduce micro-stutters during scrolling, app switching, and other everyday tasks.

Unfortunately, one familiar OnePlus feature isn’t making the transition to ColorOS. Typing “1+” followed by the equals button in the Calculator app will no longer bring up the iconic Never Settle Easter egg. It was among the little touches we highlighted when previewing what OnePlus users stood to lose with the switch to ColorOS, and OnePlus has now officially confirmed it’s gone.

items.summary: Even Galaxy Watch 4 owners aren't being left behind.

Wearables and health

Samsung is bringing Galaxy Watch 9 health features to older Galaxy Watches

Even Galaxy Watch 4 owners aren't being left behind.

•

•

•

Adamya Sharma / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

TL;DR

• Samsung is bringing six Galaxy Watch 9 health and fitness features to the Galaxy Watch 8 series.

• The upgrades include Heart Health Score, Vitals, Daily Cardio Load, Fitness Index, improved Sleep Coaching, and enhanced sleep apnea detection.

• Select features also support older models, with improved Sleep Coaching extending back to the Galaxy Watch 4.

Samsung could break its tradition of launching a new Galaxy Watch every year as early as 2027, reportedly shifting its focus to software updates and new health features for existing smartwatches. We’re already seeing what that approach could mean for Galaxy Watch owners, as Samsung has confirmed that several health and fitness features from the Galaxy Watch 9 are making their way to last year’s models.

The company began rolling out stable One UI 9 Watch to the Galaxy Watch 8 series in mid-November, with US users receiving the update shortly after. In a new announcement, Samsung has detailed six health and fitness upgrades originally introduced with the Galaxy Watch 9 and Watch Ultra 2 that are coming to the Galaxy Watch 8 and Watch 8 Classic.

Vitals tracks five overnight health metrics, including heart rate, skin temperature, and blood oxygen, to flag unusual changes in your readings. Heart Health Score, meanwhile, helps you understand how everyday habits like sleeping and exercising affect your heart. For fitness enthusiasts, Daily Cardio Load helps balance training and recovery, while Fitness Index assesses your overall fitness and suggests exercises based on your goals.

Brady Snyder / Android Authority

Samsung is also improving Sleep Coaching, which now requires just three nights of data within two weeks to offer personalized guidance. The advice adapts weekly as your sleeping habits change.

Earlier this month, Samsung began rolling out enhanced sleep apnea detection to its latest wearables, promising support for older Galaxy Watches. That upgrade is now reaching the Watch 8 series, offering three categories of breathing disruption frequency. Other additions include the Portrait Watch Face and an improved Compass that lets you save important locations and retrace your steps.

Perhaps even better, Samsung confirms that Daily Cardio Load and Fitness Index support the Galaxy Watch 7 running One UI 9 Watch, while the improved Sleep Coaching experience goes back as far as the Galaxy Watch 4.

Some features require separate updates to Samsung Health or Samsung Health Monitor, and availability may vary by region.

Whether or not Samsung skips next year’s smartwatch launch, bringing these features to hardware that can already support them gives existing Galaxy Watch owners fewer reasons to spend money on a new model.

Pixel users report broken always-on display in Android Auto after November update

Even the newest Pixel phones aren't spared.

•

•

•

Sanuj Bhatia / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Pixel users report that the November update breaks the always-on display when connected to Android Auto.

• The issue affects multiple generations, including the Pixel 9, Pixel 10, and Pixel 11 series.

• We’ve reached out to Google to see whether it’s aware of the bug and working on a fix.

Google’s November update for Pixel phones has already caused a fair share of headaches, from broken lock screen shortcuts to issues with the always-on display and notifications. It turns out the update may have introduced yet another display-related bug, this time affecting Pixel owners who use Android Auto.

Pixel owners across Reddit and the Android Auto Help community report that their phones’ always-on displays stop working when connected to Android Auto. Instead of showing the time, notifications, and other glanceable information, the screen remains completely black until they disconnect from their cars.

The issue isn’t limited to older Pixels either. While the initial complaint came from a Pixel 9 Pro owner using wireless Android Auto, the Pixel 10 Pro, Pixel 11 Pro, and Pixel 11 Pro XL are also affected.

Rita El Khoury / Android Authority

Some peculiar things are happening behind the scenes. One Pixel 11 Pro owner noticed that their phone’s display settings blamed Bedtime Mode for disabling AOD, even though neither Bedtime Mode nor Driving Mode was active.

Disabling Driving Mode hasn’t helped, and neither have recent Google Play system updates. A Pixel 11 Pro XL owner briefly regained normal AOD functionality, but the problem returned the following morning. Tapping the screen still wakes the phone, but that defeats the convenience of having an always-on display.

Similar complaints have surfaced outside Google’s English-speaking communities, with a Pixel 9 Pro owner on Taiwanese forum Mobile01 also experiencing broken AOD and having trouble getting Android Auto to launch automatically following the November update.

The good news is that an Android Auto community specialist has already requested diagnostic information from an affected user to help with the investigation. The specialist subsequently confirmed that the team had contacted the user via email for further assistance.

We’ve asked Google if it’s aware of the bug, and we’ll update this article when we hear back.

Unihertz

TL;DR

• Last week, Unihertz posted a teaser for an upcoming new Titan 2 Elite color option.

• Today the company reveals the Titan 2 Elite in white.

• Unihertz is accepting pre-orders now, but the white model won’t ship for another couple months.

Hardware keyboards are one of those holdovers from the early days of smartphones that just keep popping back up, and if you’re tempted to go a little retro for your next purchase, you’ve now got a new option available to you, as Unihertz reveals its latest color for the Titan 2 Elite.

Last week, we saw Unihertz start teasing a new color option for the Titan 2 Elite. The teaser itself didn’t seem to contain much in the way of hints, leaving us to just speculate as we waited for the announcement. At the very least, we wouldn’t have long to wait, with the manufacturer implying we’d get our answer sometime this month. December still doesn’t arrive for a few more days, but this mystery is already wrapping up, with Unihertz sharing a new white colorway for the Titan 2 Elite, joining the previously available black and orange.

Unihertz

As you can see above, this keyboard is for more than just typing, and like BlackBerry models of yesteryear, you can use the touch-sensitive surface for scrolling through your favorite apps, or even pull up a cursor for finer control.

If all those keys aren’t enough to satisfy your crave for input buttons, Unihertz even gives the Titan 2 Elite a programmable side button that you can set up as a shortcut to whatever you want.

At just about $490, the white Titan 2 Elite costs the same as the orange and black models, but there is another consideration that might impact your purchasing decision — while the other ones ship straight away, the new white edition is currently just in pre-order, and won’t ship for another two months, well into the new year.

That said, Unihertz is prioritizing shipments based on the order in which they’re received, so the longer you hem and haw about it, the further out your ship date is likely to slide.

Was this the new color you were hoping for? Will you be picking up a white Titan 2 Elite, or are you maybe still holding out hope we could get a fourth color option somewhere further down the line? Let us know down in the comments.

items.body: Apple's annual four-day Black Friday through Cyber Monday shopping event is now live in Australia , New Zealand , and Thailand , and it will continue to roll out across Europe, the U.S., and Canada as the calendar turns to Friday, November 27 around the world. In the U.S., Apple's terms and conditions say the promotion begins on November 27 at 12 a.m. Pacific Time and ends on November 30 at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time. During the shopping event, customers can get an Apple gift card with the purchase of an eligible product at an Apple Store, in the Apple Store app, and on Apple.com. However, the gift card can only be used towards future purchases, and higher immediate discounts on Apple products are frequently available at Amazon and other resellers. In the U.S., Apple is offering gift cards worth up to $300 with the purchase of an eligible iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, HomePod, AirPods, Beats headphones, Beats Pill speaker, Apple Pencil Pro, and select Magic Keyboards for iPads. For the first time ever, Apple is also offering a $25 gift card with select third-party accessories from brands including Anker, Belkin, Mophie, Nimble, Rains, and Twelve South. The selection includes chargers and MacBook covers. As usual, many of Apple's newer products are excluded from the offer, including the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone Duo, MacBook Neo, latest models of the iPad mini, Apple TV 4K, iMac, and Mac Studio, and more. The Nothing Headphone (1) stand out with a striking transparent design, but there’s plenty of substance too. They’re tuned by KEF, support Hi-Res audio, and use satisfying physical controls, including a roller and paddle, instead of fiddly touch panels. Battery life is a highlight, with up to 80 hours of playback with ANC off and 35 hours with it on. The Nothing Headphone (1) are $169 on Amazon, saving you $130 (43%) and matching their lowest price.

Beats Studio Pro
Beats Studio Pro
Spatial audio, lossless playback, and big battery life

The Beats Studio Pro are a relatively light-weight set of Bluetooth headphones. With up to 40 hours of battery life, USB Type-C charging and wired playback, as well as a 3.5mm port, ANC, and Spatial Audio, these are contenders for the hottest headphones of 2023.
See price at Amazon

The Beats Studio Pro are a great all-rounder for both iPhone and Android users, with one-touch pairing and full app support on both platforms. You get active noise canceling, a Transparency mode, Personalized Spatial Audio, and lossless audio over USB-C. Battery life runs up to 40 hours, and a quick 10-minute charge adds hours of playback. The Beats Studio Pro are $149 on Amazon, half their $299.99 list price.

Sony WH-CH730N

The Sony WH-CH730N combines effective noise canceling with a lightweight, foldable design and up to 50 hours of battery life. Clear calls, adjustable ambient sound, and quick charging make it a practical choice for work, travel, and daily listening.
See price at Amazon
Save $81.99

The Sony WH-CH730N deliver dependable noise canceling and Sony’s signature sound for much less than its flagships. Their battery life is outstanding, with up to 50 hours with noise canceling on and 75 hours without, while a three-minute charge gives you an hour of listening. They’re also lightweight at 207g, foldable, and support multipoint and Bluetooth 6.0. The Sony WH-CH730N are $98 on Amazon, an $82 (46%) discount and the lowest price we’ve seen.

JBL Tune 680NC (2026)

The JBL Tune 680NC show you don’t need to spend much for noise canceling. These on-ear headphones feature adaptive noise canceling with Smart Ambient, JBL Pure Bass sound, and multipoint connectivity, plus they fold flat for easy carrying. Battery life is huge at up to 76 hours, or 50 hours with ANC on, and a five-minute charge adds five hours of playback. The JBL Tune 680NC are $49.95 on Amazon, $60 (55%) off and the lowest price we’ve seen.

Earbuds are easier to carry everywhere, and this year’s Black Friday headphone deals include some of the best-ever prices on flagship models. There’s also a great option for anyone who just wants something cheap and reliable.

The Sony WF-1000XM6 have excellent active noise cancelation, great sound quality, and outstanding microphone performance thanks to AI-powered beamforming. The redesigned fit is comfortable and secure, though the larger size may not suit smaller ears. With 9+ hours of battery life, LDAC support for high-resolution audio on Android, IPX4 water resistance, and comprehensive app features including a 10-band EQ, these deliver flagship performance across the board.

Save $81.99

The Sony WF-1000XM6 are Sony’s latest flagship earbuds, and they’re a top pick for anyone who wants great sound and strong noise canceling in one package. Eight noise-canceling microphones and Sony’s QN3e chip help block out the world, while LDAC support gets the most out of compatible phones. The Samsung Galaxy Buds 4 Pro brings a redesigned look, along with improved ANC, head gesture support, and more seamless AI smarts.

The Samsung Galaxy Buds 4 Pro are Samsung’s best earbuds yet and the natural choice for Galaxy phone owners. A two-way speaker setup delivers excellent sound, including 24-bit/96kHz audio on supported Galaxy devices, and adaptive noise control adjusts to your surroundings. They also add head gestures, Auracast support, and an IP57 rating, with up to seven hours of playback and 30 hours with the case. Apple AirPods Pro 3
Adaptive audio and enhanced ANC.

The Apple AirPods Pro 3 are a solid update to the Apple wireless earbuds lineup. Improved ANC, IP57 ratings, plus heart rate sensor and fitness tracking built in. There's even a hearing aid mode, and improved spatial audio.
See price at Amazon

The Apple AirPods Pro 3 are the best earbuds for iPhone owners, and this is their best deal yet. Apple says the noise canceling is twice as effective as on the AirPods Pro 2, and the earbuds add built-in heart rate sensing for workouts, Live Translation, and hearing health features. They’re rated IP57 for sweat and water resistance and last up to eight hours with ANC on. The AirPods Pro 3 are down to $149 on Amazon, a $100 (40%) discount and their lowest price ever.

The Google Pixel Buds 2a are the 2025 budget-friendly Pixel Buds offering. As the smallest and lightest A-series buds yet, the Buds 2a are equipped with ANC, a twist-to-adjust stabilizer, and the Tensor A1 chipset. They integrate with Gemini AI tools, and offer an IP54 rating. Don't let the word "budget" fool you, the Buds 2a offer up to 10 hours of music playback per charge, an easily repaired charging case, Binaural audio support, and Bluetooth 5.4 connectivity with Multipoint switching.

The Google Pixel Buds 2a bring active noise canceling to Google’s most affordable earbuds, powered by the same Tensor A1 chip as the Pixel Buds Pro 2. The Beats Studio Buds Plus are good earbuds for listeners who hop between Android and iOS. Beats' active noise canceling is a step up from the original Studio Buds. Small housings and a range of ear tip options make these a joy to wear for hours at a time.

The Beats Studio Buds Plus are a versatile pair of earbuds that work equally well with iPhones and Android phones, with one-touch pairing on both. They offer active noise canceling, a Transparency mode, and clear calls thanks to upgraded microphones, plus a total of up to 36 hours of battery life with the case. The translucent design is a fun touch too. The Beats Studio Buds Plus are $89.95 on Amazon, an $80 (47%) saving and their lowest price yet.

They’re a great choice as a spare pair, a gift, or a first set of wireless earbuds. The CMF Buds 2a are $17.89 on Amazon, $11 (38%) off and the lowest price we’ve seen.

TCL TAB 10 Gen 4 hits a record low under $130

Save $50 on TCL's 10.1-inch Android tablet with 128GB of storage, now at its lowest price ahead of Black Friday.

TCL’s affordable 10-inch tablet just dropped to a new low. The TCL TAB 10 Gen 4 with 4GB of RAM and 128GB of storage is down to $129.99 on Amazon, which is $50 off its $179.99 list price. That’s $10 below yesterday’s price and $20 under the best deal we saw for it in October.

The TCL TAB 10 Gen 4 is a straightforward everyday tablet. Its 10.1-inch FHD display is a comfortable size for streaming shows, reading, video calls, and keeping recipes in view on the kitchen counter, and it runs Android with access to the Google Play Store.

The 128GB of storage stands out at this price. Plenty of budget tablets still ship with 32GB or 64GB, so having more room for downloaded movies, games, and photos makes a real difference, especially for families sharing one device.

A 6,000mAh battery should comfortably cover a day of casual use, and there are cameras on the front and back for video chats and quick snaps.

It’s a sensible pick as a first tablet for a child, a shared household device, or a simple screen for travel and bedtime streaming.

The deal comes from a third-party seller, but the order ships from Amazon. At $129.99, the TCL TAB 10 Gen 4 is one of the most affordable ways to get a 10-inch Android tablet with 128GB of storage right now.
